text:
maria: FYI — eu-west-1 had a weird tail last night. lots of small gen requests piled into the queue and our autoscale didn't keep up. latency spikes for ~6m.
chris: ugh, any indicators? was it spot churn or a sudden qps burst?
maria: not spot churn. charts show steady instance health but queue depth jumped and admission rate dropped. looks like scale decision was rate-limited by our 2m cooldown + boot latency.
devops-bot: ALERT: autoscaler eu-west-1: desired=0 -> 4, provision_time_median=82s, queue_depth_peak=118, shed_rate=12% (2160000032)
jyoti: quick thought — instead of preallocating a large warm pool, try standby orchestration + queue hinting. let the request carry a small "queue hint" that signals urgency so admission can borrow headroom credits immediately.
sam: can you sketch how that works? sounds like adding metadata to every request could complicate routing.
jyoti: short version: keep a modest warm pool, but allow short-lived speculative allocations when a hint is present. the admission controller will check headroom tokens before full instance init. if tokens available, mark request as "fast-path" and schedule a hedged probe to a standby node.
chris: example config?
jyoti: here's a rough canary config we used in staging: 
```
standby_orchestrator: 
  min_standby: 2
  headroom_pct: 0.10  # keep 10% capacity as borrowable credit
  speculative_probe_timeout_s: 6
  max_speculative_per_region: 3
  prewarm_cooldown_s: 45
```
maria: that speculative_probe_timeout is key — it hedges requests to a likely-warm node without fully counting as a long-term provision. if probe succeeds, promote; if not, fallback to normal scale.
ops-sre: cost note — speculative allocations increase short-term cost. recommend gating behind route-level policy: only high-priority routes get queue-hinting. do a 5% traffic canary.
sam: fine by me. what telemetry do we need to be confident?
maria: track probe success rate, promotion latency, and effective shed_rate change. also watch median boot time and burden on spot fallback.
chris: how to test without impacting prod customers?
jyoti: run canary in eu-west-1 on non-critical model routes first. add feature-flagged header `x-rw-queue-hint: priority=low|high`. start high only for internal traffic then graduate.
ops-sre: also add an alert if speculative_probe_promote_rate < 30% or if cost-per-token increases > 7% over baseline.
maria: action items: 1) jyoti + chris to push canary flagging and admission change (start internal) 2) sam to wire dashboards: probe_success, promote_latency, speculative_cost 3) ops-sre to add budget guard and alerting. I'll coordinate rollout and set canary window to 72h.
chris: I'll prep the feature flag PR. will include unit for admission logic and e2e that simulates queue flood.
jyoti: I'll drop the staging runbook and config into the canary PR.
ops-sre: set budget guard to auto-disable spec alloc if cost delta > 9% (conservative).
maria: thanks. FYI we should avoid changing global cooldown timers for now — prefer targeted speculative path. simpler rollback. :thumbsup:
devops-bot: DEPLOY-PLAN: canary: eu-west-1 (internal routes only) -> monitor 72h -> auto-rollout decision based on alerts (2160000144)
chris: cool. ping me if you want me to shepherd the rollout tonight.
maria: will do. thanks everyone.
